definition: Generating a natural-language description of what a SQL query computes — the inverse of text-to-SQL.
details: Generating a natural-language description of what a SQL query computes — the inverse of text-to-SQL. It aids query explanation, documentation, and debugging.

explainer.lead: SQL-to-Text generates a natural-language description of what a SQL query computes, the inverse of text-to-SQL. It matters for explaining, documenting, and debugging queries that are hard to read.

tiers.eli5: It's like having someone read a dense recipe aloud in plain words so you understand what dish it actually makes.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to turn complex queries into explanations for documentation or review. A pitfall is that a fluent description can sound correct while misrepresenting subtle logic such as joins or filters.
tiers.paperLevel: A natural-language generation task that maps a SQL query to a textual account of its computation, serving as the inverse of text-to-SQL.

explainer.example: For a query joining orders and customers and filtering on region, the output might read: 'Lists each customer in a region with their orders.'
